title: Yearbook and Mixtape
premise: Ines Hartwell has spent senior year keeping her head down, counting days until she can escape her fractured home and the small town of Marrow Creek. But when her debate rival Theo Vasquez becomes her partner for a semester project documenting the town's shuttered community center—the place that once hosted every mixtape night, yearbook signing, and found-family gathering in town—she uncovers plans to demolish it before graduation. Forced to work with Theo and an unlikely crew of classmates, Ines must rally the town to save the center, discovering along the way that belonging isn't something you wait for; it's something you build. The story ends on graduation day, with the center saved as a youth collective, Ines finally winning the argument at home by choosing to stay connected rather than disappear.
about_author: Yara Thornbury is a former high school debate coach who spent a decade watching teenagers argue their way into selfhood. She writes from a converted garage studio filled with thrifted yearbooks and unlabeled cassettes.

chapters.title: The Argument She Keeps Losing
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Opening at a debate tournament she wins easily, then cutting to a dinner-table fight with her mother about moving away after graduation, establishing her invisibility strategy at school and her restlessness at home. Mr. Okafor announces the paired semester project: Ines is matched with Theo Vasquez, her smug rival, to document the closed Marrow Creek Community Center. Emotional beat: resentment and dread.

chapters.title: Dust, Tape Hiss, and Old Signatures
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Ines and Theo. Exploring the abandoned center, they find a 1998 time capsule: yearbooks, mixtapes, photos of their own parents as teenagers—friends, once, before some falling-out neither will explain. They interview townsfolk who light up remembering the center's mixtape nights. Ines learns demolition is scheduled for June, weeks after graduation. Emotional beat: reluctant wonder turning to alarm.

chapters.title: Everything We Didn't Say
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, climax. Their exhibit of recovered memories goes viral locally, but the town council meeting to approve demolition looms—and Ines discovers her mother was the one who petitioned to close the center years ago, after a grief-fueled falling-out with her best friend, Theo's aunt. At the council meeting, Ines uses every debate skill she has, and for once argues not to win but to heal, playing her mother's old mixtape aloud. Emotional beat: raw confrontation and catharsis.

chapters.title: Signed, Sealed, Still Playing
chapters.summary: Theo's POV closing into shared narration. The council grants the center reprieve as a student-run youth collective; Ines's mother and Theo's aunt reconcile over the time capsule contents. On graduation day, the class buries a new time capsule—including Ines and Theo's project and a fresh mixtape. Ines chooses a local college, realizing home was never the prison; silence was. Emotional beat: belonging, bittersweet hope.
